chapter: Theaters, the Navy and the Singletons' partnership
title: The Savoy Ballroom: dancing, Count Basie and the bouncers
summary: Zutty and Marge recall Ethel Waters and Louis dancing at the Savoy, taking Jimmy Dorsey there, and Count Basie asking if he would beat him to Europe. The bouncers were ex-fighters.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Ethel Waters used to go up there and dance her brains out.
And Louis and Ethel used to go up there and dance their brains out. Louis was a good dancer you know.

They would take old Jimmy Dorsey up there one night, yes. We were coming out of the Raxy Theater and he said, where are you going? And I said, we are going up to the Savoy to hear Count Basie. And then that's when we were leaving the next day for Europe. And old Count Basie say, you going to beat me over there? I say, I'm leaving
tomorrow. (LAUGHTER). Yes, this cut wanted to know if I was going to beat him over there. I said, I'm leaving tomorrow.
Well that was a, I mean there's another thing about it, you know, the way it was run. It was good wasn't it? I mean you had a big crowd but there was no nonsense.

The nonsense there was too much man. A lot of ex-fighters you know, as bouncers in that joint. And then if you got thrown out the last foot you felt was the doorman George ( right in the butt, you see. He didn't miss, you see because (?). Boy that was something. Everybody used to go there.
We'd go over Sunday night if you weren't working.
